## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical experience with image provenance, SBOMs, and policy enforcement in GPU-enabled Kubernetes at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Cosign signing with repository public key
- SBOM generation and verification (e.g., SPDX/SBOM formats)
- Central provenance record and digest alignment
- Kyverno or OPA gate policies for admission control
- CI integration (GitHub Actions) and runtime validation

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal GitHub Actions workflow sketch
name: Sign and Verify Image
on: [push]
jobs:
  sign-verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Build image
        run: |
          docker build -t registry.example.com/project/model:tag .
      - name: Sign image
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/project/model:tag
      - name: Verify image
        run: cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/project/model:tag
```

- How would you handle rotation of the cosign public key in a live environment?
- What performance impact would SBOM generation introduce in CI and how to mitigate it?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked

This question evaluates a candidate's ability to design enterprise-grade, policy-driven security controls across hybrid Kubernetes environments. It tests practical knowledge of admission controllers, supply chain security, and multi-cloud consistency—skills essential for platform engineers and security architects.

## Key Concepts

### 1. Image Provenance and Digest Pinning
Digest pinning ensures immutable deployments by locking images to specific content-addressable hashes (e.g., `sha256:abc123...`). This prevents supply chain attacks through tag manipulation. The policy requires images to be referenced by digest rather than mutable tags like `latest` or `v1.2.3`.

### 2. Sigstore Attestations
Sigstore provides cryptographic verification of software supply chain provenance. By validating attestations against allowed signers, organizations ensure that only images built and signed by trusted parties can be deployed. This integrates with the Sigstore transparency log for auditability.

### 3. SBOM Validation
Software Bill of Materials (SBOMs) provide a complete inventory of components within an image. Combined with vulnerability scanners like Grype, this enables organizations to enforce baseline security requirements—such as no critical vulnerabilities or specific library versions—before deployment.

### 4. Pod Security Standards
The policy enforces Pod Security Standards by blocking privileged containers, hostNetwork access, and hostPath volumes. These controls prevent container escape scenarios and limit the blast radius of potential compromises.

## Evaluation Criteria

Strong candidates will demonstrate:
- Understanding of OPA Rego syntax and Gatekeeper constraint templates
- Knowledge of Sigstore's keyless signing and verification workflows
- Familiarity with SBOM generation and vulnerability scanning tools
- Ability to design policies that are both restrictive and operationally practical
- Consideration for multi-cloud and on-premises consistency

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design runtime security controls that span CI, policy engines, and multi cloud networking, ensuring outbound traffic is strictly controlled and auditable.

## Key Concepts

- Policy-as-code (Gatekeeper/OPA)
- Egress gateway design and TLS origination
- Outbound allowlist management
- CI validation for policy enforcement
- Cross-cloud consistency and testing

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate for Gatekeeper enforcing egress gateway annotation
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8segressgateway
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sEgressPolicy
  targets:
  - target: obj  # pseudo example for clarity
    rego: |
      package k8segress
      default deny = true
      deny[msg] = msg {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.metadata.annotations["egress.gateway/enforced"] == "true"
        msg := "Pod must set egress.gateway/enforced=true to route via central gateway"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint demonstrating allowlist usage (illustrative)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sEgressPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-egress-gateway
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        kinds: ["Pod"]
  parameters:
    allowlist: ["app.allowed.example.com"]
```

```yaml
# Failing manifest (no egress annotation or disallowed destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: bad-egress-pod
  annotations:
    # missing or false
    egress.gateway/enforced: "false"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing manifest (annotation set and allowlisted destination)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: good-egress-pod
  annotations:
    egress.gateway/enforced: "true"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: nginx:1.23.4
```

## Local and CI Validation

- Local: run gatekeeper locally to test ConstraintTemplate/Constraint; simulate Pod admission with k8s manifest.
- CI: run a workflow that lints manifests, validates policy via a test cluster or KinD, and fails on noncompliant manifests.

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: ImageSBOMAttestation
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: ImageSBOMAttestation
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package imagesbomattestation
      
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.object.metadata.namespace != "monitoring"
        container := input.review.object.spec.containers[_]
        not valid_image(container.image)
        msg := sprintf("Container image %v fails SBOM/attestation validation", [container.image])
      }
      
      valid_image(image) {
        has_attestation(image)
        no_high_severity_vulns(image)
      }
```

questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked
- Tests policy-as-code skills for multi-tenant Kubernetes environments
- Evaluates ability to translate security requirements into enforceable runtime and CI gates

Key Concepts
- Kyverno, Pod Security Standards, Resource limits, CI gates, Drift detection

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-secure-deployments
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  background: true
  rules:
  - name: security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must define a secure securityContext with runAsNonRoot: true, readOnlyRootFilesystem: true, and drop all capabilities"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: "true"
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: "true"
                  capabilities:
                    drop: ["ALL"]
  - name: require-resources
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validate:
      message: "Each container must specify resource limits and requests"
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - resources:
                  limits:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
                  requests:
                    memory: "?*"
                    cpu: "?*"
```

Failing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: insecure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: insecure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
```

Passing Test Manifest
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: nginx:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
        resources:
          requests:
            memory: "64Mi"
            cpu: "250m"
          limits:
            memory: "128Mi"
            cpu: "500m"
```

CI Validation Steps
```bash
# Install Kyverno CLI
brew install kyverno

# Validate policies against manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest deployment.yaml

# CI/CD integration example (GitHub Actions)
- name: Validate Kubernetes manifests
  run: |
    kyverno apply policy.yaml -f deploy/
```

Runtime Gate Demonstration
```bash
# Apply the policy cluster-wide
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Verify policy is active
kubectl get clusterpolicy require-secure-deployments

# Attempt to deploy non-compliant manifest (will fail)
kubectl apply -f insecure-deployment.yaml
# Error: Validation failed: Each container must define a secure securityContext...

# Deploy compliant manifest (will succeed)
kubectl apply -f secure-deployment.yaml
# deployment.apps/secure-app created
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests a beginner-friendly, practical security gate focused on container runtime privileges in Kubernetes manifests.

## Key Concepts
- PodSecurityContext vs Container securityContext
- readOnlyRootFilesystem, runAsNonRoot, runAsUser
- PrivilegeEscalation and privileged flag in containers
- GitHub Actions as a gating mechanism

## Code Example
```yaml
# Failing manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: fail
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:latest
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: false
          runAsUser: 0
          privileged: true
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: true
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
```
```yaml
# Passing manifest
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: pass
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: example/app:1.2.3
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 1000
          privileged: false
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```
